# TFT companion audit — Carousel-Companion.html

**File audited:** `~/workspace/user/files/Carousel-Companion.html`
**Date:** 2026-11-21 · **Size:** 7.8 MB (8,133,298 bytes), 2,335 lines, 29 `<script>` blocks
**Title in file:** "Carousel — TFT Item Companion" (line 1). Brand in UI: "Carousel".
**Method:** static analysis only — Python/grep/chunked reading, JSON-parsing the three bundled data blobs. No runtime execution, no live fetch test, no browser run. Anything marked "to verify at runtime" was not observable statically.
**Do not edit the HTML from this report alone** — the fixes below are a Codex work plan (§9), not edits.

## Verdict (read this first)

This is a much more careful tool than its description suggests — and its own code comments are unusually honest about its limits. It is **not** a comp recommender that picks "the best S/A comp" from live tier lists. It is:

1. **A manual item tracker** (its real core, lines 627–676, 434–513): queue of target items, loose-component bench, craft/receive/restore, undo, backup export/import.
2. **An Academy comp importer / plan tracker**: paste a TFT Academy team code → exact-match a guide → track its items on a board (lines 880–977, 1299–1356).
3. **An "Explore builds" fit-ranker** (CompFinder, lines 1361–1547): ranks all 45 Academy guides by a transparent heuristic against what the user typed in (units + stars, completed items, loose components, first augment). Academy tier leads; fit breaks ties inside a tier, with a narrow promotion rule.
4. **A MetaTFT per-champion 3-item-build supplement** (lines 1006–1156): S/A *item builds for one champion*, used only to adjust/pivot individual champions — never to pick a comp.

**The three claims in the brief that do not survive the audit:**

| Brief claim | What the code actually does |
|---|---|
| "Recommends the best S or A tier comp" | Bundled Academy snapshot has **zero S-tier guides** (A 9, B 18, C 11, X 7 — §2). There is no S comp to recommend from Academy. MetaTFT S/A are 3-item builds for a single champion (246 S / 489 A of 15,550 builds), not comps. The ranker returns *all* tiers, tier-led. |
| "Not built for a specific patch, pulls live data at runtime" | Half true. Live refresh exists (§2), but the bundled snapshot is **Set 18 / Patch 18.3b, fetched 2026-10-01**, the core recipes are hardcoded, MetaTFT bundled data is **Patch 18.3 (not 18.3b)** with no patch-equality check, and refresh only fires on launch / new game / paste-code. If live fetch fails, it silently falls back to the stale snapshot. |
| "Carousel priority factors in drop odds" | **No drop-odds model exists.** The code says so three times (lines 516–517, 545, 1162, 1942). Carousel ranking is marginal-utility gain from a beam search (§4) plus a *loot-history tie-break* (which components dropped from PvE before, in this game only). No percentages, no stage-refill or carousel-odds model anywhere. |

**Biggest single correctness risk:** the recommender's inputs are whatever the user typed, and several of its most important signals are weak or missing — no stage/round, no gold, no HP, no streak, no lobby/contest, no level. A comp can rank #1 on an empty board (alphabetical A-tier, §3.7). The promotion rule, the X-tier handling, and the emblem/augment gating each have inconsistencies (§3.8) that can produce exactly the "wrong recommendation" Evan reported.

**Biggest structural risk:** everything is one 7.8 MB file, 4.9 MB of it base64 Academy icons, with **no tests at all** (only `Tracker` and `PivotPlanner` have `module.exports` guards, lines 461/721, and nothing imports them). Every scoring constant is a magic number inline. Any patch change rots the bundled snapshot, the hardcoded role table, and the regex heuristics together, with nothing to catch it.

## 1. What the app is — layout, panels, user flows

Single self-contained HTML file, dark theme, `max-width: 1840px` (line 98), responsive down to ~430 px (media queries lines 5, 7, 29–30, 109, 123, 135, 140, 148). No build step, no framework, no service worker, no backend, no account. State is `localStorage` only (keys §7).

### 1.1 Shell (line 638, the `app` innerHTML)

- Top bar: "Carousel" + "Ctrl + V anywhere to import" + Help button + (later) Data & keys / utility menu (lines 2255–2266).
- Academy bar (lines 909–912): link to `https://tftacademy.com/tierlist/comps` + status text `Updated <date> · Patch <patch>` (lines 915–920) + MetaTFT status (line 1115).
- Workspace grid: left column (item picker), centre column (queue + plan), right column (component bench / shopping list). At ≤680 px it collapses to one column (line 29).

### 1.2 Panels and flows

| Panel / flow | Where | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| **Item picker ("Choose your items")** | lines 639–642, 723–809 | Search by name/role/component; filter by component; 39 core craftable items only (see §4 — emblems/radiants/artifacts are *not* in this picker). Click adds a copy to the queue. `/` opens the drawer, hover shows recipe. |
| **Queue / targets** | lines 643–656, 2270–2332 | One card per target item: icon, holder (early → final champion), recipe slots (green = component reserved), Make / Restore / Pivot / drag-reorder (keyboard: Space + arrows + Enter, Esc cancels). Drag changes presentation order only; `QueueOrder` (lines 589–624) keeps a separate `recommendedOrder`. |
| **Component bench** | lines 651, 979–998 | 10 components with +/− counters (keys 1–8 for the first 8; Spatula/Pan have no key). "In hand" strip. `LootTracker.gain/remove` records the *source* of each loose copy (loot / carousel / other, lines 529–541). |
| **Shopping / carousel priorities** | lines 649–650, 1931–1976 | "Still missing from your queue, after your bench" — replaced at render time by `DecisionUI.drawCarousel` (§4). Pin (★) re-ranks within a group. |
| **Completed strip** | lines 992–996 | Done items; click to assign a holder champion (lines 1310–1316). Holder assignment is what lets MetaTFT reason about equipped items. |
| **Craft now / Received item** | lines 819–844 | "Craft now" chips for items whose recipe is fully owned; "Received item" completes a target without spending loose components (carousel/anvil drops). |

Exact champion-set match only; if several guides share the code, highest tier then most recently updated wins (`QuickImport.choose`, lines 884–885). Replaces unfinished targets, keeps bench + completed items. On no exact match it refreshes Academy data and retries once (lines 949–953). |
| **Board / plan overview** | lines 1299–1356 | 4×7 hex board from the guide's `boardIndex` values (unplaced units listed separately), Academy tips (Build + Stages 2–4, lines 1339–1340), "Reset targets to Academy", MetaTFT connection diagnostics. |
| **Explore builds (CompFinder UI)** | lines 1818–1927 | The actual recommender UI. Inputs: current champions (+ stars), first augment (2-1 only, §5), completed items (incl. emblems/radiants/artifacts via Browse-all). Output: ranked list of all 45 guides, top 5 + "All N comps", "Aim here" loads the guide. Hidden once a comp is active unless "Explore builds" is toggled (lines 1900–1903). |
| **MetaTFT S/A builds dialog** | lines 1159–1244 | Per-champion table of S/A 3-item builds (tier / avg place / games), filterable by contained item and by "match completed items". "Pivot to an item…" opens the champion pivot dialog. Also an in-app iframe of metatft.com (lines 1169, 1222–1225) with a new-tab fallback. |
| **Champion pivot** | lines 1931–2012 | For one champion, list every item that sits in a compatible S/A MetaTFT build alongside equipped items; Plan pivot / Build now / Use owned. A pivot target stays locked (`pivotIntents`, lines 1571, 1618) until built/removed/released. |

"Mark made" executes the batch as one undoable transaction (`DecisionPlanner.execute`, lines 1659–1671). Tempo toggle Balanced / Need strength now (line 1999). |

### 1.3 State shape

`state` (line 632, cleaned lines 466–485): `queue[]` (uid, item, academyItem, planSource academy/meta/manual, done, received, champion, earlyChampion, sourceComp, sourceURL, used, usedSources, recommendedOrder), `owned{}` (component counts), `pins[]`, `currentUnits[]` (apiName + stars, max 28), `chosenAugments[3]`, `firstAugment`, `augmentOffers{round, ids[3], seen[]}`, `pivotIntents{}`, `tempo` (balanced/urgent), `lootHistory{complete, counts, loose}`, `lootTieBreak`, `activeComp{guide, id, title, code, itemPriority[]}`.

**Not tracked (and the recommender therefore cannot use):** game stage/round beyond augment round, player level, gold/econ/interest, HP, win/loss streak, carousel round/position, lobby/contest, shop contents, orb/anvil history beyond the loot-source log. The DecisionUI comment (line 1930) admits this: "no round, HP, gold, carousel position or offer transcription."

### 1.4 Help text is honest

The in-app Help (line 638, `<dialog id="help">`) says: "This is a manual tracker. No live-game connection or API key is used… TFT Academy data refreshes automatically when you open the app or start a new game. If offline, the saved snapshot stays available." That matches the code. The footer (line 638) credits "Core recipes · CommunityDragon data · Sep 23, 2026" — but CommunityDragon is **only a footer link** (`https://raw.communitydragon.org/latest/cdragon/tft/`); no CommunityDragon fetch exists in the file. The core recipes in `DATA` (line 222) are hardcoded, not fetched from CommunityDragon.

## 2. Live data — every fetch, parse, cache, fallback

There are exactly **two** `fetch()` call sites in the file (plus none for images beyond `<img src>`). No proxy, no API key, `credentials:'omit'` on both.

### 2.1 TFT Academy — guide/tierlist snapshot

**Endpoints (lines 408–423, `Academy.refresh`):**

- `GET https://tftacademy.com/tierlist/comps/__data.json` (or `/tierlist/comps/set<set>/__data.json` when a specific set is requested)
- `GET https://tftacademy.com/api/assets/champions?set=<guideSet>`
- `GET https://tftacademy.com/api/assets/items?set=<guideSet>`
- `GET https://tftacademy.com/api/assets/augments?set=<guideSet>` (failure tolerated — `.catch(()=>null)`, line 416; then line 418 reuses the old augment list if the set matches)

Timeout 15 s via `AbortController` (line 409). No retry, no back-off, no manual refresh button.

**Parsing:** the `__data.json` endpoint is a SvelteKit payload: `{nodes:[{data:[...index-based graph...]}]}`. `Academy.unpack` (lines 241–257) dereferences the index graph (max 100,000 reads, blocks `__proto__`/`constructor`/`prototype` keys). If the shape changes it throws "TFT Academy changed its data format. Your saved snapshot is still available." `Academy.normalize` (lines 273–284) then:

- takes `set = max(guide.set)` across guides; keeps only guides with `isPublic && set === that max && finalComp` is an array;
- drops any guide/champion/item field not in its whitelist (`cleanGuide`, lines 267–271 — truncates text to 4,000 chars, caps altBuilds 40, carousel 30, finalComp 28, augments 60, tips 12);
- **throws if guides/champions are empty or guides > 500 / items > 1,000** (line 282).

**Item mapping (`Academy.register`, lines 288–304):** Academy `apiName`s are mapped to the hardcoded `DATA` items by *normalized name* (lowercase, strip non-alphanumerics). If a name matches, the live `composition` overwrites the hardcoded recipe when it is exactly 2 known components. If not, a new `Academy_<apiName>` item is appended with `recipe` if craftable, otherwise `recipe: []`, `special: true`, `academyOnly: true`, icon = bundled base64 if present else `https://assets.tftacademy.com/items/<apiName>.webp`. Consequence: **a live refresh can add new items, but only into the `academyOnly` pool** — they never appear in the main picker (which filters `!i.academyOnly`, lines 640–641, 741).

**Caching:** `localStorage['carousel-academy-v7']` (line 229). On load, a cached snapshot replaces the bundled one unconditionally if it has guides/champions/items and an integer `set` (lines 426–431) — **no age/TTL check, no set check against anything**. On successful refresh it is overwritten (line 420). The bundled snapshot is the fallback for everything.

**Refresh triggers:** `void refreshData()` on launch (line 976), on `carousel-new-game` (line 972), and once after a failed exact code match (lines 949–953). There is no user-visible "refresh now" control and no refresh on focus/online (unlike MetaTFT, §2.2). Concurrent refreshes are de-duplicated (`refreshTask`/`refreshSet`, lines 928–942).

**Patch/set detection — verified against the user's statement:**

- Bundled snapshot (line 224): `patch:"18.3b", set:18, updated:"2026-09-30 21:33:53.721Z", fetchedAt:"2026-10-01T00:44:26.432Z"`. So as shipped on 2026-11-21 the bundled data is **~7 weeks old**.
- Live refresh derives the set from the data (`guideSet = max(set)`, line 414) and rejects a mismatch if a set was requested (line 415). `normalize` records `patch` from the payload's `patch` field (line 277).
- **But:** nothing validates that the live patch is the patch the user is playing, and nothing warns when the bundled patch (18.3b) is stale — the status line just prints whatever `snapshot.patch` says. A paste-code for a different set is rejected with a clear error (`Academy.match`, line 311: "This code is Set N; the loaded tierlist is Set M"), which is good — but only for the import path, not for Explore/manual entry.
- The `guideHex` helper (lines 305–308) hardcodes an exclusion for `TFT16_AnnieTibbers` — a Set 16 leftover in Set 18 code. Harmless today, emblematic of rot risk.

### 2.2 MetaTFT — per-champion item-build statistics

**Endpoints (lines 1132–1134):**

- `GET https://api-hc.metatft.com/tft-stat-api/unit_detail_overall?unit=<apiName>&queue=1100&patch=current&days=3&rank=CHALLENGER,DIAMOND,EMERALD,GRANDMASTER,MASTER,PLATINUM&permit_filter_adjustment=true`
- `GET https://api-hc.metatft.com/tft-stat-api/unit_detail_items?unit=<same>&...&num_items=3`

i.e. ranked queue 1100, current patch, last 3 days, Platinum+, 3-item builds. Timeout 15 s, max 3 concurrent (`active>=3`, line 1129), freshness 15 min (`freshness=15*60000`, line 1088), error back-off 5 min (line 1121), re-check every 60 s while visible + on focus/online (lines 1142–1143). Only champions actually assigned to a queued item are requested (`checkActive`, line 1141; `render` line 1144).

**Compaction (`MetaBuilds.compact`, lines 1010–1032)** — this re-implements MetaTFT's own scoring from raw placement distributions, it does not consume a MetaTFT tier directly:

- Only `levels` rows with `lvl_items == [<=4, 3]` are used; `count`/`mean` placement computed from them.
- Per build: `games = sum(places)` (8 placement buckets), `avg = total/games`, `variance`, `confidenceAvg = avg + 1.282*sqrt(variance/games)` (one-sided ~90% upper bound), `comparison` = mean placement of everyone *not* playing this build, `popularity = min(1, sqrt(games/count/.01)) * (items.length/3)^2 / (30 if ThiefsGloves else 1)`, `score = (.5-(confidenceAvg-comparison))*.7*popularity*(games/popular)^.1`.
- Scores are then **rescaled** so the 3rd-best build is 0.35 (`scale = .35/third`, lines 1028–1030), and tiered: `S >= .35, A >= .25, B >= .15, C >= .05, else D`.
- Builds kept only if exactly 3 items and `games >= 30` (line 1031).

This rescaling means **"S" is relative within a champion** (top-3 builds get pushed toward S), not an absolute quality bar, and not comparable across champions. The file never claims otherwise in code comments ("Confidence, frequency and tier normalization follow the unit page's model", lines 1006–1008) — but the UI labels them plainly "MetaTFT S/A" with no such caveat.

**Bundled MetaTFT snapshot (line 1002):** `updated: 1790213163275` (= 2026-09-24), 57 units, all `patch:"18.3"`, 15,550 builds total (101–429 per unit). Build tiers: S 246, A 489, B 1,289, C 4,768, D 8,758. **Patch is 18.3, not 18.3b** — and no code path checks MetaTFT patch against Academy patch. `MetaBuilds.ranked` / `dataFor` check only `data.set === 'TFTSet' + Academy.snapshot.set` (lines 1039, 1181, 1575). A stale-patch MetaTFT build can therefore supplement a current-patch Academy plan with no warning. The reference dialog does display `patch ${data.patch}` (line 1195), so the mismatch is visible if the user looks.

**Caching:** `localStorage['carousel-metatft-v2']` (line 1087), seeded from `META_BUNDLED`, then newer entries replace older by `updated`. Validation on load is strict (3 string items, finite score, tier in S–D, line 1092). On live success the whole cache is re-saved filtered to the current set (line 1137); quota failures are swallowed. Status text (line 1115): "live stats" / "live + cached stats" / "cached stats" / "cached · refresh unavailable" / "awaiting champion".

**Failure mode:** on fetch error the connection is marked with the error (`'Timed out'` or `'Network / CORS unavailable'`, line 1138) and the UI keeps using bundled/cache. There is no CORS proxy anywhere in the file. Both live sources are direct cross-origin fetches; if either host blocks the origin (notably when the file is opened via `file://`, where `localStorage` and CORS behave differently per browser), the app degrades to bundled data with only the small status line as a signal. **To verify at runtime:** open the file over plain HTTP(S) vs `file://` and watch the Academy/MetaTFT status lines + the diagnostics panel (lines 1306–1307, 1343–1345).

### 2.3 What is *not* live

- `DATA` core items/components (line 222): hardcoded, 10 components + 39 items, footer-dated "Sep 23, 2026". Recipes are only overwritten by a live Academy refresh when the Academy name matches (see §2.1).
- Champion/item/augment **icons**: 341 `data:image` URIs embedded in the file (§7); live snapshots use remote `assets.tftacademy.com` URLs instead (lines 280, 558, 1366).
- No BunnyMuffins, no CommunityDragon, no Riot API, no other source. `bunnymuffins` appears **0 times** in the file.

## 3. Recommender logic (CompFinder) — exact scoring and where it goes wrong

Entry point: `CompFinder.ranked(plan)` (lines 1508–1523) → `evaluate(plan, guide)` per guide (lines 1453–1499). Inputs are only what the user entered in Explore: `currentUnits` (+stars), completed items (`queue.done`), loose components (`owned`), first augment (+ chosen augments), and tempo. **Unbuilt wishlist items do not count** (only `queue.done` is matched in `evaluate`, line 1457; pending items are used only as "remaining" targets).

### 3.1 The formula

```
score = tierScore + fitScore
tierScore: S 12, A 10, B 8, C 6, D 4, X 8   (line 1495; unknown tier 0)
fitScore = min(96, itemScore)
         + min(36, componentScore)
         + min(36, matchedAugments * 24)          // 0 / 24 / 36 (max 2+ augments counted? no cap on count, cap is 36)
         + board.unitScore                          // ≤ 44 + 8 + 3 = 55
         - min(18, unmatched * 6)                   // off-plan completed *craftable* items only
         - requirementPenalty                       // emblems/augment gating (§3.4)
         - executionPenalty                         // missing core units (§3.5)
selectable = build.entries.length > 0 && build.missing.length === 0   (line 1498)
```

**Sort** (`ranked`, line 1522): unblocked first, then `recommendationTierRank`, then `fitScore` desc, then base tier, then title A–Z. `recommendationTierRank` starts as the Academy tier rank (S 0, A 1, B 2, C 3, D 4, **X 2** — line 1500) and can be *promoted* by `strongFit` (§3.6).

### 3.2 Item scoring (`evaluate`, lines 1455–1481)

Completed items are matched greedily in queue order against the guide's remaining build entries:

- Exact/equivalent match (radiant counts for its base via `Academy.baseItem`, lines 260–266; `itemMatches` line 266): **+24 if priority < 3, else +18**; **emblem match +40**. `priority` is the entry's index in `Academy.build(guide).entries` order (which is itself Academy priority order, §3.3).
- Radiant-instead-of-base: **+6 extra** and recorded as a "Radiant upgrade" special match (line 1463).
- Featured item (`guide.mainItem`) owned: **+12** (lines 1479–1481). Note `mainItem` is null for most guides (only ~half have one; §2 data), so this is often a no-op.
- Unmatched completed items are then tried as **special carriers** (`specialCarrier`, lines 1393–1419): an emblem/radiant/artifact is worth **+32 (emblem alt) / +28 (special alt) / +22 (special on core) / +12 (special non-core) / +18 (non-special alt) / +8 (core) / +5 (non-core)**, plus the carrier's stars — but *only* if the item is an Academy alternate for that unit, in the Academy item guide's `recommendedChampions`, or in an S/A MetaTFT build (≥100 games) for that champion. Otherwise it falls through to the early-comp pool (**+10** if it matches an early-board item for a non-final unit, lines 1475–1476) or to `unmatched` (craftables, −6 each) / `unknownSpecial` (non-craftables, **no penalty**).
- Slot accounting: `slotCost` is 3 for Thief's Gloves, 1 otherwise (line 1392); a champion's items cannot exceed 3 slots. Unique items cannot duplicate on one champion (lines 1398–1399); emblems are not placed on a champion that already has that trait (line 1400).
- **MetaTFT substitution inside scoring** (lines 1483–1492): after matching, for each champion with placed items, if the Academy baseline is *not* completable from equipped items, `DecisionPlanner.builds(virtual…)[0]` (best S/A Meta build) replaces that champion's remaining entries. This is the one place MetaTFT changes a comp's *remaining* items during ranking. It is subtle and untested (see §3.8).

### 3.3 Item order / build construction (`Academy.build`, lines 323–359)

`build(guide)` flattens `finalComp` items (main champion first, line 325) into entries, then re-orders by the guide's `carousel` (Item Priority) list: each listed item promotes one copy; component-only priority lists instead use the guide's early-board items first, then favour recipes using preferred components (lines 343–357). Items in `finalComp` that have no `itemMap` entry are reported in `missing` — and any guide with `missing.length > 0` is **not selectable** (line 1498). With the bundled data this never triggers (all finalComp items map), but after a live refresh that adds an unmapped item it silently drops the whole guide from Explore.

`Academy.itemizationOrder` (lines 360–380) parses the guide's `augmentsTip` prose with a regex for `item priority: A > B > C` (2–6 groups). Anything not matching that exact pattern returns `[]` — prose, conditions and ambiguous roles are explicitly not guessed (comment lines 361–362). This parsed order drives carousel holder ranking (§4.3).

### 3.4 Emblem / augment gating (`requirements`, lines 1420–1437)

- Emblems in the final comp (plus emblem alternatives from `altBuilds`): owned → consumed from the bank; craftable (2-component recipe, components available in `pool`) → `craftableEmblems`; otherwise → `missingEmblems`. Penalty: `min(60, missing*24)`, plus **+40 and `blocked=true`** if the guide is tier **X** and its `mainAugment` is not held. Only 6 guides have a `mainAugment` at all (Yi Rengar, Solar Melee, Solar Kayle, Trait Ladder, Unrivaled Reroll, Adaptor Reroll — and three of those are just Portable Forge).
- `blocked` is also set when the tip matches `/only play[^.!?]*emblem/i` and emblems are missing (line 1435). This regex is fragile: "Only play when you have emblem for Rengar" matches; "Only play from early win streak and lots of gold" (Draven AD 9) correctly does not — but only because "emblem" happens not to appear in that sentence. Any rewording breaks it either way.
- Emblems that are *not* in `finalComp` items but are needed for a trait breakpoint are not checked at all.

### 3.5 Board fit (`boardFit`, lines 1374–1390) and execution (`execution`, lines 1438–1452)

- Final-comp unit owned: points `[0,2,7,15][stars] × (1.5 if core)` + 8 if a core 3-star target is owned at 3★. Core = main champion or a unit with ≥2 items in the final comp (line 1380). Capped at 44.
- Early-comp unit: `[0,.5,2,4][stars]`, capped at 8. Trait bridge (≥2 traits shared with the final comp, not in final/early): 0.5/1 per unit, capped at 3.
- **Traits are opaque Academy IDs** (`c.traits`, e.g. `y5fv8ap9m6nn5yr`) compared against the final comp's champions' trait IDs (line 1376). This works only while the snapshot is self-consistent; a live refresh that re-issues trait IDs invalidates saved `currentUnits` matching silently (matching is by `apiName`, so units still match — only the *trait* bridge breaks).
- Execution penalty: for the top-3 core units (main first), missing a 3★ target costs 1.5–3, missing a 4/5-cost entirely costs 5/8, etc., capped at 18 — **then multiplied by `boardCoverage = min(1, owned.size/4)`** (lines 1450–1451). With 1 unit entered the penalty is quartered; with 0 units it is **zero**. The comment (line 1449) says this is deliberate ("sparse item entry does not establish that the whole future board is missing") — but it means early-game, low-information states are systematically under-penalised for missing cores.

### 3.6 Promotion (`strongFit` + `ranked`, lines 1501–1522)

A comp can move up the tier bands only if *all* of: `finalItems >= 2`, or (≥1 final item + ≥1 upgraded core), or a 3★ upgraded core, or ≥3 upgraded keepers; **and** `fitScore >= 60`; **and** not blocked, no missing emblems, no missing augment. Then, per tier skipped, it must beat the best fit in the target tier by **30 fit points** (`fitScore < max(other.fitScore) + 30*(tiers skipped)` stops promotion, lines 1516–1520). This is a stable-band design (comment lines 1513–1515) — good — but note the 30-point bar is on `fitScore`, which excludes `tierScore`, while the *displayed* sort uses `recommendationTierRank` first. A promoted B comp and a native A comp with equal fit are ordered by `fitScore`, not by evidence strength.

### 3.7 Concrete wrong-recommendation modes

1. **Empty / near-empty input → alphabetical A-tier.** With no units, items, components or augment, every guide scores `tierScore` only (fitScore 0, no penalties — execution penalty is 0 because `boardCoverage` is 0). All 9 A guides tie at 10, then sort by `fitScore` (0), base tier, then **title A–Z**. #1 is therefore "Ahri Morgana" / "Aphelios Rapidfire" / "Ashe Juggernauts" by alphabet, not by data. There is no "not enough information" state; the UI presents it as "Closest routes from what you have" (line 1824). A first-time user with an empty board gets a confident-looking #1 that means nothing.
2. **No S-tier exists, but the UI language implies S/A selection.** The reference dialog is titled "MetaTFT · S/A item builds" (line 1167) and the finder says "badges = Academy rank" (line 1824) — but Academy's top band in the bundled data is A. A user hunting for "the S comp" will never find one, and nothing explains why. If a live refresh later *does* return S guides, `tierScore`/`tierRank` handle S — but `QuickImport` does not (§3.8.3).
3. **Tier dominates fit by construction, and the gap is small.** `tierScore` spans only 8 points (A 10 vs C 6, X 8 = B). A single emblem match (+40 itemScore, capped in the 96 bucket) or two matched augments (+36) can swamp the tier gap — which is *intended* by the promotion rule, but only via the 60-point / 30-per-tier gates. Outside promotion, a B comp with fit 59 vs an A comp with fit 0 still loses (tier first). That is a defensible design choice, but it means the ranker can recommend a comp the user has *nothing* for over one they are halfway into, whenever the tier differs and fit < 60. The threshold (60) is not surfaced in the UI.
4. **Augment match is binary and coarse.** `matchedAugments.length * 24`, capped at 36 (line 1496): one matching augment is worth more than most item matches. But matching is against the guide's 8 listed augments + `mainAugment` only (line 1494). A guide whose augment list is stale/missing (live data) loses 24–36 points for no in-game reason. Conversely, holding a *bad* augment for a comp costs nothing — there is no negative augment signal in CompFinder (negatives live only in AugmentAdvisor, §5).
5. **Off-plan items are penalised asymmetrically.** An off-plan *craftable* costs −6 (capped −18); an off-plan radiant/artifact/emblem with no supported carrier costs **0** (`unknownSpecial`, line 1477) and is shown as "No supported match" without affecting rank. So a board holding a random artifact looks *more* compatible than a board holding a random craftable. The direction of that asymmetry is backwards from what a player would expect.
6. **Early-comp credit is thin and half the guides have no early items.** 21 of 45 guides have **zero** items in `earlyComp`; 17 have 2, the rest 1–4. `earlyMatches` (+10) and `earlyScore` (cap 8) therefore fire unevenly by guide, not by game state — a data-coverage artefact, not a signal.
7. **Duplicate / variant champions.** Academy has 72 champions for ~65 names (variants: `DA_18_Akali_AD`, `DA_18_MasterYi_AD`, `DA_Nidalee18_AP`, `DA_18_KhaZix` vs Lunarwood, plus 7 cost-0 entries: Elderwood summons + `TFT_Flex_Lv7–10`). `CompFinder.champions()` filters `cost > 0` (line 1372), but `MetaBuilds.champion(name)` matches by *normalized name* and takes the first hit (line 1033) — a name with two variants can silently resolve to the wrong `apiName`, and then `dataFor` looks up the wrong MetaTFT unit. `guideHex`/`match` also treat flex/level champions as real units (they are in the snapshot; `match` requires ≥60% shared hexes, line 319).
8. **Component-fit beam is greedy in a subtle way.** `componentFit` (lines 1524–1535) enumerates, per remaining entry, which of its 2 components are owned (mask 0–3), weight `max(1, 4 − n*0.5)` (early entries worth more), +2 if both owned, beam width 40 deduped by pool signature. It counts each loose component once (correct), but it **ignores special items entirely** (recipe length ≠ 2 skipped, line 1527) and it scores *remaining* entries only — completed items already matched are excluded, so a comp whose remaining items share components with already-owned items gets no extra credit for that overlap. It also treats all components as equally obtainable; a Sword and a Spatula are weighted identically.

### 3.8 Bugs / inconsistencies found (by severity)

| # | Issue | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| B1 | **X-tier ranked inconsistently in three places.** `tierRank`: X = 2 (between A and B, line 1500). `tierScore`: X = 8 = B (line 1495). `QuickImport.choose`: tier map `{S:0,A:1,B:2,C:3,D:4}` has no X → `?? 9`, so an X guide sharing a team code sorts **last** (lines 884–885). Same comp, three different tier meanings depending on entry path. | Lines 884–885, 1495, 1500 |
| B2 | **Empty-state recommendation is alphabetical, not "unknown".** See §3.7.1. | Lines 1450–1451, 1508–1522 |
| B3 | **MetaTFT patch never checked against Academy patch.** Bundled Meta is 18.3, Academy is 18.3b; `ranked`/`builds`/`dataFor` check only `set`. | Lines 1039, 1181, 1575; data §2 |
| B4 | **PivotPlanner role table covers only the 39 core items** (line 681). Every `Academy_*` item (emblems, artifacts, radiants, new craftables) gets profile `['flex']` (line 685). In `suggest(role:'similar')` they share a role with nothing except Thief's Gloves, so per-item pivots for special items are driven almost entirely by component coverage (`covered*18 + overlap*4`, line 704), not by role. | Lines 679–711 |
| B5 | **`Academy.build` drops a guide from Explore if any finalComp item is unmapped** (`selectable` requires `missing.length === 0`, line 1498). After a live refresh that introduces an item the mapper cannot resolve, the whole comp disappears from the ranker instead of being shown with a warning. | Lines 327–331, 1498 |
| B6 | **Emblem `blocked` depends on prose regex** `/only play[^.!?]*emblem/i` (line 1435). Rewording a tip flips gating. Also, `requirements` only inspects emblems listed as finalComp *items*; trait-breakpoint emblems that are not itemised are invisible. | Lines 1420–1437 |
| B7 | **Augment `tier` is Academy-internal (1/2/3), but AugmentAdvisor reroll logic compares it as rarity** (line 2090: same `tier` required for a reroll alternative) while the UI badge maps it to Silver/Gold/Prismatic (line 2116). If Academy's tier numbering ever diverges from rarity, both break together. | Lines 2089–2090, 2116 |
| B8 | **Backup export can exceed its own import cap.** Export embeds `Academy.snapshot` verbatim (line 858); before any live refresh that snapshot is the bundled one *with* base64 icons (~4.9 MB). Import rejects text > 5,000,000 chars (lines 863, 873). A first-run backup is therefore likely un-importable. *To verify at runtime: export before refreshing and check the file size.* | Lines 858, 863 |
| B9 | **Stale `localStorage` Academy cache has no TTL and no set check on load** (lines 426–431). An old cache from a previous set silently replaces the bundled snapshot and is only corrected if a live refresh succeeds. | Lines 426–431 |
| B10 | **Name-based champion resolution can pick the wrong variant** (see §3.7.7). `MetaBuilds.champion` (line 1033), `PlanAdvisor`/`DecisionPlanner` name matching, and the reference dialog's name-deduped champion list (lines 1174–1178). | Lines 1033, 1175 |
| B11 | **`componentFit` and `Tracker.allocate` both assume queue order = priority order**, but `allocate` iterates `state.queue` order (line 438) while the displayed order is `recommendedOrder` after `QueueOrder.ensure` (line 645). They coincide only because `QueueOrder.apply` physically reorders `plan.queue` (line 615) — a future change to either breaks component reservation silently. | Lines 438, 615, 645 |
| B12 | **Loot source attribution is FIFO** (`LootTracker.take` shifts the loose array, line 541). If a component was gained from loot and then from carousel, crafting attributes the loot copy first regardless of which the player actually spent. Cosmetic for the tie-break, but the "source" labels in the UI present it as fact. | Line 541 |

## 4. Item system — components, full items, artifacts, radiants, anvils, carousel, drop odds

### 4.1 The item universe

- **Hardcoded core (`DATA`, line 222):** 10 components (`BFSword, RecurveBow, NeedlesslyLargeRod, TearOfTheGoddess, ChainVest, NegatronCloak, GiantsBelt, SparringGloves, Spatula, FryingPan` — `componentOrder`, line 629) and **39 full items, all with exactly 2-component recipes** (verified by parsing: recipe-length counter `{2: 39}`). That includes `TacticiansRing / ForceOfNature / TacticiansScepter / ThiefsGloves` (Spatula/Pan recipes) — so "special" in the tracker is not "non-craftable", it is "Academy-only / no 2-component recipe".
- **Academy catalogue (line 224):** 139 items — components 10, craftables 39, **radiants 36, Ornn/artifacts 32, emblems 21, others 1** (Golden Item Remover). Emblem composition: 16 have 2-component recipes (craftable), 5 have none (augment-granted, e.g. `DA_18_EmblemFloraFatalisAugment`). Radiants/artifacts have no composition — they can never be crafted from components, only received.
- **Name matching is punctuation-insensitive** (`normalizeName`, line 230), which correctly reconciles `Warmog's Armor` (Academy) with `WarmogsArmor` (DATA) and `Tactician's Crown/Shield` likewise. Credit where due.
- **The main picker shows only the 39 core items** (`!i.academyOnly`, lines 640–641, 741). Emblems, radiants and artifacts can enter the tracker only via: Academy import, Explore "owned items" (Browse all, lines 1855–1860), an anvil "Took this" (§4.4), or "Received item". A user who opens the app and wants to type "I have a Radiant Guinsoo's" cannot do it from the primary UI. That contradicts the brief's "you can enter your items" for the special categories.

### 4.2 Tracking correctness (`Tracker`, lines 434–460; `OfflineTracker`, lines 465–513)

- `Tracker.allocate`: walks the queue top-down, reserves owned components per recipe slot, reports `needs` (component → count + which items need it + earliest rank). Each component counted once — correct. Duplicate-recipe items (Blue Buff = Tear+Tear, Deathblade = Sword+Sword) are handled by `recipeCounts` (line 486) in `canCraft`.
- `Tracker.complete` consumes owned components in recipe order and records per-component source via `LootTracker.take`; `restore` returns them (lines 450–459). `OfflineTracker.receive` completes without spending components (line 509) — correct for carousel/anvil receipts.
- `craftOptions` (lines 488–500) lists craftable queued items *and* their conflicts (two items needing the same scarce component) — good, and the UI surfaces it as "Craft now".
- **Edge:** `allocate` reserves for *pending* items only; completed items' `used` components are already deducted from `owned` at completion time, so no double-count — but if a user manually edits `owned` after completing items, `restore` returns `used` counts that may no longer match reality (no reconciliation).

### 4.3 Carousel priority (`DecisionPlanner.carousel`, lines 1713–1747; `carouselTargets`, 1672–1712)

For each of the 10 components (Spatula/Pan only if needed or a pivot target exists — line 1732; the no-queue fallback `discovery` uses only the first 8, lines 1748–1764):

1. `planned[id]` = queued items still missing that component (after bench), with champion + rank.
2. `pivots[id]` = components that would complete an *alternative* S/A MetaTFT build for a champion in the queue (`carouselTargets` reserves components for retained targets first, lines 1689–1690, then attributes missing components to changed items).
3. **Score (planned need):** `gain + min(20, reach) + 3 − priority*0.15`, where `gain = solve(owned + 1×id) − solve(owned)` — the increase in the whole-bench beam-search score from having one more of that component — and `reach = Σ 3*max(1, 6−rank)` over targets. `solve` is the §6 beam search.
4. **Score (pivot-only):** S 20 / A 10 + `min(2, score)` − `min(6, missing)*0.1` (line 1743).
5. **Sort** (line 1746): components with `count > 0` first, then pins, then carrier rank (only if both have count), then score, then loot tie-break, then `componentOrder`.

**What this is:** a marginal-utility ranking — "which component most increases the value of what I can craft next, given my queue and my pins." That is a reasonable definition, and the beam-search `gain` is the most sophisticated part of the file.

**What it is not:** drop odds. There is no carousel-odds table, no per-stage drop table, no "probability this component appears on the next carousel" anywhere. The only probabilistic-adjacent logic is `LootTracker.compare` (lines 542–547): *if* the loot history is complete (game tracked from the start), *and* the tie-break is enabled, *and* both components are among the first 8, then prefer the component with more prior natural PvE drops — explicitly "not a verified current-set probability model" (line 517) and "no percentages, stage refill assumptions, or promised future drops" (line 545). The UI repeats the disclaimer (lines 1162, 1942). **The brief's "factors in drop odds" is therefore a feature to build, not a feature to fix** — see §8/§9 for what a real model would need (per-stage carousel composition is not public data; the honest version is a stated prior, not a claimed odd).

**Other carousel gaps:** no carousel *round* input (the app never asks which carousel it is, so it cannot know how many picks remain or that later carousels offer full items/champions); no "which components are already on the carousel" transcription; `discovery` (no queue) scores components against the top 8 ranked comps with `ready ? 6 : 1` per item (lines 1752–1760) — a much cruder path that runs exactly when the user has entered the least.

### 4.4 Anvils (`DecisionPlanner.anvil`, lines 1765–1801; `AnvilUI`, lines 2171–2253)

Five tabs (line 2172): Components / Artifacts (`ornns`) / Completed (`craftables`) / Radiant (`radiants`) / Emblems (`emblems`).

- **Component anvil:** reuses the carousel ranking (§4.3); "Took this" records the component with source `'other'` (line 1793 — correctly *not* counted as a PvE drop).
- **Other types:** every item of that Academy type is scored against the active guide (or top-8 ranked guides if no comp is active): **exact Academy target 55 / alternate 47 / Academy-item-guide endorsement 32 / no match 0**, +3 if it is the guide's main champion's item, ± fit adjustment if no active comp (lines 1781–1785). If a comp *is* active, a MetaTFT S/A pivot can also score it: **S 62 / A 53 + `min(3, score)` + retained** (line 1788) — note this can outrank an exact Academy target (55), which is intended (Meta evidence beats a static list) but is not explained in the UI.
- **Gaps:** scoring ignores games/avg-place entirely (an S build with 100 games and one with 10,000 games score the same except via `score`'s `min(3,…)` term); it ignores whether the item's *components* are available (correct for an anvil — you take the finished item — but the "reason" text doesn't say that); emblem slot/trait checks use the champion's `traitKeys` (line 1776) — correct. Note the anvil *does* see Academy-only items: `ownedCatalog()` maps `DATA.items`, and `Academy.register` appends `Academy_*` items into `DATA.items` (lines 300, 425), so registered Academy craftables appear in the Completed tab — unlike the main picker, which filters them out (§4.1). The remaining gap is that an item added by a *live refresh* only appears after `register` runs, and an item the mapper cannot resolve never appears at all.
- **Offer comparison** (AnvilUI `compare` mode): entering offers does not change inventory; "Take this" is recommended only when the top offer is strictly best and supported (`supported`, `tied` logic, lines 2207–2214). Ties are called out rather than broken silently — good. But the verdict for a single offer is just "1 offer entered — add the others" (line 2210): the app will not recommend from a single anvil offer even when it is obviously best, which is over-cautious for a 1-option anvil (some anvils offer 1 item).
- `receiveAnvil` (lines 1792–1800): completes an exact queued target if one exists for the suggested champion, otherwise pushes the item as **unassigned** completed (`champion:''`). Unassigned completed items are invisible to MetaTFT reasoning until the user assigns a holder — a silent loss of signal that the UI does not flag.

## 5. Augment suggestions (AugmentAdvisor, lines 2018–2105; AugmentUI, 2108–2166)

**Input:** user types 3 offered augment names per round (2-1 / 3-2 / 4-2; `stages`, line 2019). Round defaults to the next unrecorded augment (line 2023). "Enter reroll" replaces one offer and records it in `seen` (line 2158). "Took this" records the pick into `chosenAugments` (lines 2099–2104) and clears offers for the next round.

**Catalog/eligibility:** `catalog(plan, round)` (line 2027) = Academy augments not already held whose `stages` include the round (augments with no `stages` — 7 in the bundle — are eligible for every round, line 2026). Note the first-augment picker in Explore (`CompFinder.augments`, line 1363) is separately filtered to 2-1 only.

**Scoring (`evaluate`, lines 2033–2079)** — a points ledger with reasons:

| Signal | Points |
|---|---|
| Academy featured augment for the active comp (`mainAugment`) | +58 |
| Academy recommends it for the active comp (in guide's 8) | +42 |
| No active comp: best endorsing ranked route, closeness-scaled | +14 + closeness×20 (max 34), + up to +9 if that route fits owned units/items |
| Mentions an owned item *and* buffs holders | +12 |
| Mentions a queued item *and* grants items/anvil | +9 |
| Offers a needed component (by name in description) | up to +10 |
| Shop/reroll wording + reroll-style comp | +8; XP wording + fast-8/9 style | +8 |
| Duplicator/reroll wording + unfinished 3★ target | +5 |
| Delayed payoff while tempo=urgent | −12; rewards-losing while urgent | −8; gives up carousel choice while components needed | −8; transforms upgraded units | −10; duplicate Omnivamp | −3 |

**Verdict (`compare`, lines 2080–2098):** Take if best ≥ 38 and evidence ≥ 2; Lean if evidence > 0 and score ≥ 8; Reroll if the weakest offer has evidence > 0 *and* (conflict or score < 20) *and* an unseen same-tier alternative scores ≥ best+16 and ≥ 32; otherwise Unknown ("No clear pick or reroll edge. Missing matches do not mean these augments are bad."). The reroll hint itself says the replacement is not guaranteed (line 2131).

**Coverage gaps / bugs:**

1. **No MetaTFT augment statistics at all.** The AugmentUI method note (lines 2113–2114) says so: "Existing MetaTFT item evidence contributes through comp fit; these are not MetaTFT augment statistics." Every augment judgement is Academy endorsement + description regexes. An augment that is statistically strong but not in any Academy guide's list of 8 scores ~0 and gets "Limited evidence" — which the UI correctly labels, but which makes the advisor useless for exactly the augments a player is unsure about.
2. **Description regexes are the whole "understanding".** Item references require the item name (>5 chars) to appear verbatim in the *description* (lines 2054–2055); component aliases cover only the 8 non-Spatula/Pan components (lines 2059–2060); "reroll"/"fast 9"/"XP" are substring tests on the guide's `style` string (line 2062). Augments whose value is in numbers (e.g. gold thresholds, stack counts) are invisible. A renamed/reworded augment silently loses all its points.
3. **Thresholds are arbitrary and uncalibrated.** 38 / 8 / +16 / 32 have no validation against any outcome data. The +58/+42 Academy endorsement dwarfs everything else, so the advisor mostly restates "take the augment your Academy guide lists" — which is already shown in Explore as a ★ (line 1911). Its marginal value over the guide list is small.
4. **No reroll-count, stage, or rarity awareness beyond `tier`.** The advisor does not know how many rerolls the player has left, that 4-2 offers are higher rarity on average, or that some augments cannot appear at some stages except via the Academy `stages` list (which is itself source data, not game rules). The `seen` list prevents re-suggesting a rerolled-away augment as an *alternative* (line 2086), but the alternative pool is the whole catalog, not the actual reroll pool.
5. **First-augment vs chosen-augment desync risk:** `heldAugments` (line 1362) prefers `firstAugment` over `chosenAugments[0]`; both are written together in the two UI paths (lines 1831, 2102), but a backup edited by hand (or an old backup) can disagree, and the advisor silently uses one.
6. **Augment data staleness:** 261 augments in the bundle, tier distribution 1:70 / 2:119 / 3:72 (Academy's internal tier, not rarity — see B7). If a live refresh drops the augment list (the `.catch(()=>null)` path), the old list is reused only if the set matches (line 418); otherwise the advisor has no catalog at all and every offer is "unavailable".

---

## 6. Pivot logic — how alternatives are ranked when exact items aren't hit

There are **three different pivot engines**, and which one runs depends on where the user clicks. This is the most confusing part of the file for a user, and the most likely source of "wrong" pivots.

### 6.1 Per-item pivot (`PivotPlanner`, lines 679–721 + dialog lines 768–796)

`PivotPlanner.candidate` scores a replacement item as `fit*10 + covered*18 + overlap*4` (line 704), where `fit` = shared role tags (important roles 5, others 3) + 5 if the candidate's first role matches the original's first role; `covered` = recipe components already owned (counting the *available* pool after reserving components for earlier queue items, lines 687–691); `overlap` = recipe components shared with the original item. `missingRole` (important roles the candidate lacks) is computed (line 702) but **never used in the score** — it is only data. `alreadyPlanned` (line 703) is also computed and never used in the score. Role tags come from the hardcoded 39-item table (line 681) — see B4: special items have no real tags.

**Ordering in the dialog** (lines 775–778): if the target has a champion, results are re-sorted by MetaTFT rank (`MetaBuilds.ranked`, §6.2) *first*, discarding the similarity score order except as a tie-break within the same Meta rank (items with no Meta rank sort last at 999). If no champion, similarity order stands. So the same item can pivot differently depending on whether a holder was assigned — correct in spirit (champion-specific evidence should win) but invisible in the UI.

### 6.2 MetaTFT champion pivot (`MetaBuilds.ranked`, lines 1036–1070; `suggest`, 1071–1081)

For a queued item on a named champion, with equipped items as commitments:

- Only builds with tier S/A and `games >= 100` (`strongOnly`, line 1050).
- The build must contain the equipped items (`fits(mapped, equipped)`), must not require more copies of the original item than equipped+planned, must not depend on an unowned non-craftable (artifact/radiant/emblem) item (lines 1055–1057), and the replacement item must be in the build alongside equipped.
- One best choice per replacement item (`best` map, lines 1064–1065); sort by tier, then Meta score, then planned matches, then games, then name (`compare`, line 1070).
- **Hard gates that produce silence:** if the champion already has 3 equipped items → `[]` (line 1045); if the target is special/academyOnly or has no champion → the Meta path is skipped and the generic similarity path is used (lines 1073–1080) — but only if the original item is *craftable from owned components* (`OfflineTracker.canCraft`, line 1073). If it is not craftable and has no champion, `suggest` returns null and the queue card shows **no pivot at all**, with no explanation.
- `MetaBuilds.suggest` (the inline "Build instead" on a queue card, lines 1105–1110) additionally requires `craftableOnly:true` — so a Meta pivot that needs a component the user does not own is never shown inline, even though the carousel could supply it next round. The full pivot dialog does not have this restriction (it shows `covered`/`missing` per candidate).

### 6.3 Whole-bench pivot (`DecisionPlanner.builds / solve / applyBuild`, lines 1573–1671; `PlanAdvisor.suggest`, 1804–1815)

- `builds(plan, name)`: all S/A Meta builds (≥100 games) compatible with equipped items, slot cost ≤ 3, remaining items all craftable (unless the pivot item itself is special and explicitly chosen), de-duplicated by sorted item set. Utility: `tier S 12 / A 9 + clamp(score,-1,1)*4 + retained*1.8 − missing*(urgent 2.2 / balanced 0.65)` (line 1591). Note `score` here is the rescaled Meta score (§2.2, range roughly 0–0.5), so the `*4` term contributes at most ~2 — **tier and retained-count dominate; the Meta score itself barely matters**.
- `groups` (lines 1621–1632): per champion, baseline Academy option + top 6 Meta options (filtered to those fitting `pivotIntents`); unassigned items get a trivial single-option group.
- `solve` (lines 1633–1658): beam search (width 64, deduped by component pool) over which craftable items to make *now*, jointly across champions: `crafts*(urgent 42 / balanced 28) + crafts*max(1, 12−group.rank) + matching*4 − meta penalty (urgent 2 / balanced 8) + min(2, score*2)`. Only the first 6 ready crafts per group are considered (line 1640). `execute` validates the whole transaction on a copy before writing (lines 1659–1671) — good.
- `PlanAdvisor.suggest` (the board's adjustment panel, lines 1804–1815): fires only when equipped items *deviate* from the Academy baseline (`subtract(baseline, equipped) === null` means deviation, line 1809) and the best Meta option is not already the current plan (within a 2-missing-component tolerance, line 1812). Otherwise it returns null and the Academy plan stands — even if a Meta build is slightly better. This conservatism is deliberate ("Academy is the baseline", line 1247) but means the advisor often says nothing.

### 6.4 Pivot gaps

- **No comp-level pivot.** All three engines pivot *items within a champion* (or within the active comp). There is no "I can't hit this comp, which *other comp* should I play instead?" path except re-running Explore manually — and Explore re-ranks from scratch, discarding the sunk cost of completed items except as matched points. The brief's "intelligently pivot to alternative builds that are S or A tier" is therefore only half built: item pivots yes, comp pivots no (except by hand).
- **Pivot intent locking is per-champion-name, not per-item** (`pivotIntents[normalizeName(name)]`, lines 1571, 1618). Pivoting one item on a champion locks that champion's remaining targets to builds containing the pivot item; pivoting a second item on the same champion silently replaces the first intent (`keepIntents:false` in `pivot`, line 1598).
- **Stale Meta data can lock in a bad pivot:** `builds()` uses whatever is in cache (bundled 18.3 data included) with no freshness check beyond the fetch scheduler. A pivot chosen from 3-day-old data is presented identically to a live one; only the reference dialog shows the snapshot date.
- **The three engines can disagree with each other** (similarity vs Meta rank vs whole-bench utility) on the same item, with no reconciliation or explanation of which won. The pivot dialog shows a "MetaTFT S/A" badge when a Meta rank exists (line 782) and nothing otherwise — the user cannot tell whether the order they see is similarity or statistics.

---

## 7. Robustness / completeness gaps

### 7.1 Performance — where the 7.8 MB goes

| Line | Bytes | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| 222 (`DATA`) | 979,330 | 10 components + 39 items, each with a base64 PNG icon (49 images) |
| 224 (`ACADEMY_BUNDLED`) | 4,947,228 | 261 augments + 45 guides + 72 champions + 139 items, most with base64 WebP icons (291 images) |
| 1002 (`META_BUNDLED`) | 1,892,523 | 57 units × 101–429 builds (15,550 builds, no images) |
| 2–221 (CSS) | ~87,000 | ~220 lines of CSS, incl. responsive rules |
| Rest (JS + HTML) | ~224,000 | All logic + the shell HTML (line 638) |

- **341 `data:image` URIs** are parsed and decoded on every load. The live Academy snapshot (after refresh) uses remote icon URLs instead, so the bundled icons are dead weight after the first successful refresh — but they are still downloaded and parsed every time the file opens.
- `render()` re-renders the queue, catalog, bench, board, finder and carousel on every mutation (each `render` wrapper re-defines and chains the previous one — at least 8 chained `render` redefinitions across the file). `DecisionUI.get()` caches by `JSON.stringify(state)` signature (lines 1943–1947), which is the main mitigation; but `CompFinder.ranked` re-evaluates all 45 guides (each running `componentFit` beam + optional Meta substitution) on every keystroke in Explore, and `MetaBuilds.ranked` scans up to 429 builds per champion per call.
- No virtualization, no lazy loading except augment icons (`loading="lazy"`, line 1367). The MetaTFT iframe (1400 px wide, line 1169) is created once and re-used — fine.
- **To verify at runtime:** load time / parse time on a mid-range phone, and whether `localStorage` quota errors appear after MetaTFT caching (the Meta cache re-save at line 1137 can exceed quota; failures are swallowed).

### 7.2 Stale data / rot

- Bundled Academy 2026-09-30 / Meta 2026-09-24 / core recipes "Sep 23, 2026" (footer) — all predate this audit (2026-11-21) by ~8 weeks. A new patch makes the bundled snapshot wrong in every direction at once (tiers, items, augments, recipes), with the only in-app signal being the small "Updated … · Patch …" line.
- Hardcoded per-patch knowledge: `DATA` recipes, `PivotPlanner.roles` (39 items), `componentOrder`, AugmentAdvisor regexes, DecisionPlanner/CompFinder magic numbers, `TFT16_AnnieTibbers` exclusion, `TFTSet18` string checks in ~57 places. A Set 19 update is a hand-edit across all of them, with no test to catch a miss.
- **No tests.** `grep` for test scaffolding: none. Only `Tracker` (line 461) and `PivotPlanner` (line 721) are written to be importable in Node (`typeof module !== 'undefined'`); nothing imports them. Every other module is DOM-coupled at definition time. The two `module.exports` lines are the seed of a test harness Codex should grow (§9).

### 7.3 Error states (mostly good, with holes)

Good: Academy format-change error with bundled fallback (line 242); code-length/set-mismatch errors (lines 234–236, 311–314); import validation with clear messages (lines 466–485, 862–869); storage-unavailable warning (lines 653–654); MetaTFT per-champion error display (lines 1113–1116, 1343–1345); "No matching S/A builds" empty states (lines 1207, 1989); tied-offer verdicts (§4.4).

Holes: Academy refresh failure shows only `refreshNote='offline / unavailable · saved data'` in the status line (line 938) — no toast, no banner, no retry button; a user who never looks at the status line will not know they are on 7-week-old data. MetaTFT failure is similarly quiet (status text only). `Academy.refresh` has no retry and no way to force a refresh except New Game / paste-code. If `localStorage` is full, `save()` sets `storageOK=false` (line 657) but the Academy/Meta cache writes fail silently.

### 7.4 Accessibility / mobile (strengths + gaps)

Strengths: `focus-visible` outlines, `aria-label`/`aria-pressed` throughout, keyboard drag-reorder, dialog focus management, `prefers` nothing? — no `prefers-reduced-motion` handling (there are `.16s` transitions, line 2) — minor. `pointer:coarse` rules give 44 px targets in places (line 142). Board cells shrink to 8 px names on mobile (line 109) — barely readable; the reference table hides item names under 540 px (line 123). The layout is desktop-first (1840 px max, two-column centre at ≥1240 px) and collapses acceptably, but the primary in-game use (phone beside the game / second monitor) is a narrow portrait viewport the CSS handles only by stacking — the queue, board and bench become a very long scroll. No "compact in-game mode".

### 7.5 What the file is *not*

Not an overlay, not connected to the game client, not an API client with a key — it is a browser tab the user consults between rounds. Any "in-game" framing for the gaming hub should say that plainly (the Help text already does). It also has no multiplayer/lobby awareness and no persistence beyond the browser (backup file is the only portability).

## 8. BunnyMuffins opener integration — the no-AI design

### 8.1 What the source actually is (verified 2026-11-21/22)

`https://bunnymuffins.lol/openers` — "TFT Opener Guide Set 18", header patch **18.3b**. Text content is a decision tree, not a table:

- **Broken Openers — Hard Force:** Aphelios Flex, Invoker Ahri Morgana, Azir Reroll.
- **Conditional:** emblem → comp (Invoker / Executioner → Flora Malphite or Draven Fast 9 / Juggernaut → Juggernaut Flex / Defender → Defender Cassiopeia Rengar / Rapidfire → 5 Rapidfire Aphelios / Hunter → Primal Malphite / Brawler → Adaptor Master Yi Reroll); 8+ winstreak → Dragon / Ashe / Draven Fast 9.
- **Reroll Check:** Veigar 2 + slam; Guinsoo's + Caitlyn; Ornn + frontline slam; AP artifact; Kha'Zix orb; Azir orb + Rod; Scuttle Crab + Riftbeast.
- **Lose Streak:** 2-1 econ augment → play for a strong Stage 4 comp (Malphite variants); strong directional augment on 3-2 (emblems, artifacts, random-output augments).
- **Augment-specific:** Expedition, Prismatic Ticket, Branching Out / Spreading Roots / Legion of Threes / Trait Tree, Portable Forge / Living Forge (data-check artifacts, hard-force ≥4.5), Worth the Wait I/II (per-hit unit tables), URF / URF's Gambit, No Scout No Pivot, Early Learnings, Solo Plate, Seraphim's Staff, Expected Unexpectedness / Birthday Reunion.
- **Econ augments:** raw gold vs units vs rerolls vs XP, each with named examples and when to take them.
- **Items:** Shojin's "best item in the game" for flexibility; Gargoyle's / Warmog's best tank slams; Deathblade / Rabadon's as stat sticks; Sterak's; shred > sunder (Kog'Maw). **Components: Sword, Rod, Belt highest priority.** "Don't be afraid to slam aggressively."
- **Win streak:** checklist (strong item slam on a 2★, upgrades, item/combat augment, scouting for 3+ rounds); comps to play from winstreak: Flora Malphite, Juggernaut Flex, Dragon/Ashe/Draven Fast 9, Invoker Ahri Morgana, Primal Malphite, Aphelios Flex. Item-thinking: keep a premium component open for carousel (Kraken's vs Giant Slayer example), build role-equivalents (Deathblade instead of Kraken's).
- **Unit priority Stage 1:** 1-costs (Akali/Camille S — Ravager sustain, hold any offensive slam; Cinderling premium AD holder, Karma AP counterpart; Rakan/Yorick 3-trait; Juggernaut frontline → premium line), 2-costs (LeBlanc/Teemo AP holders, Scuttle Crab enables Riftbeast, Caitlyn Guinsoo's holder), 3-costs (Kha'Zix orb → reroll, Cassio premium AP holder, Krug Riftbeast/taunt, Diana Ravager, Azir reroll, Rengar econ+AD holder).
- **Lose streak:** only 3 reliable plans from a weak opener (econ augment 2-1; emblem/Solar stabilise Stage 4; save HP Stages 3–4); full loss streak "generally not good", mix streaks, farm 1 turn of 6+ loss if forced; loss-streak comeback = carousel priority (higher-quality items, high-roll units), greed BIS, spike Stage 3/4. If loss-streaking with no condition: Primal Malphite or Aphelios Flex (Nidalee stabilises Stage 4).
- **Generic openers:** 2 Ravager + Front; 3 Blossom + 2 Juggernauts; 4 Ravager; Riftbeast Gromp; 2 Hunter + Front; Rengar Orb; Elderwood Rapidfires; 2 Spellweaver + Frontline; 3 Sprykin; Kha'Zix Orb — **each with a "Comps to play" list**. Crucially, the *boards themselves are images* (Images 6–15, `bunnymuffins.lol/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/…png`); the text does not list the units on each board. The 1/2/3-cost hold tiers and the item-priority list are also images (Images 2–5).

**Metadata warning:** the page footer says "Master every opening strategy for TFT Set 16" and "Updated: 2026-10-26" — stale boilerplate that contradicts the Set 18 / 18.3b header. Do not trust page metadata; the header + a human read are the source of truth. There is **no API, no JSON, no RSS** — the page is a WordPress post. Any "live" integration is therefore a *curated snapshot*, exactly like the existing Academy/MetaTFT bundled snapshots, not a live fetch. Scraping the HTML at runtime would be fragile (WordPress markup, image-embedded data) and would still miss the boards.

### 8.2 Recommended design (no LLM at runtime)

**Principle:** the opener is a deterministic rule engine over data the user already enters, plus two *new* inputs the current app lacks (streak + HP/level are optional; streak is required for the BunnyMuffins rules to fire). Same pattern as `AugmentAdvisor.evaluate` and `CompFinder.requirements` — data in, points/reasons out, no model call.

**New data file (per patch, versioned, human-curated):** `openers/<patch>.json`, e.g. `openers/18.3b.json`:

```json
{
  "patch": "18.3b", "set": 18,
  "source": "https://bunnymuffins.lol/openers",
  "sourceUpdated": "2026-10-26", "curatedAt": "2026-11-2x", "curatedBy": "human",
  "itemPriority": { "components": ["BFSword","NeedlesslyLargeRod","GiantsBelt"],
                    "slam": [{ "item": "SpearOfShojin", "rank": 1, "note": "best item, flexible AD/AP holders" }] },
  "unitHolds": { "1": [{ "unit": "DA_18_Akali_AD", "tier": "S", "holds": ["AP","AD"], "note": "Ravager sustain" }] },
  "rules": [
    { "id": "emblem-invoker", "kind": "conditional",
      "when": { "emblem": "DA_18_EmblemInvoker" },
      "then": { "compIds": ["<academy-guide-id: Ahri Morgana>"], "plan": "hard-force", "priority": 1 },
      "sourceRef": "Conditional: Invoker Emblem?" },
    { "id": "reroll-caitlyn", "kind": "reroll-check",
      "when": { "item": "GuinsoosRageblade", "unit": "DA_18_Caitlyn", "unitStars": 2 },
      "then": { "compIds": ["<academy-guide-id: Caitlyn Hunters>"], "plan": "reroll", "priority": 1 },
      "sourceRef": "Reroll Check: Guinsoo's + Caitlyn?" },
    { "id": "winstreak-8", "kind": "streak",
      "when": { "streak": { "type": "win", "min": 8 } },
      "then": { "compIds": ["Dragon 9","Ashe Fast 9","Draven AD 9"], "plan": "fast-9", "priority": 2 },
      "sourceRef": "Conditional: 8+ Winstreak?" }
  ],
  "genericOpeners": [
    { "id": "2-ravager-front", "name": "2 Ravager + Front",
      "board": [{ "unit": "DA_18_Akali_AD" }, { "unit": "DA_18_Camille" }],
      "leadsTo": ["<academy guide ids>"], "notes": "Akali any damage (prefer AP); Camille consistent AD holder" }
  ],
  "loseStreak": { "when": "no direction + econ augment 2-1",
                  "plan": "Play for Stage 4 stabilisation (Malphite variants / Solar); save HP Stages 3-4; carousel priority is the comeback mechanic; greed BIS, spike Stage 3-4",
                  "fallbackComps": ["Primal Malphite","Aphelios Flex"] },
  "unmapped": ["Blossom Ahri"]
}
```

Rules:

1. **Curate, don't scrape.** A human reads the guide each patch (including the image boards — transcribe the units on each generic-opener board and the hold tiers from Images 2–5 into `genericOpeners[].board` and `unitHolds`), writes the JSON, and records `unmapped` — BunnyMuffins comp names that have no Academy guide (e.g. "Blossom Ahri" vs Academy "Spirit Blossom" / "Ahri Zyra"). **Comp identity is an explicit map `bunnymuffins name → Academy guide id`, never fuzzy name matching** (names differ: "Dragon Fast 9" vs Academy "Dragon 9", "5 Rapidfire Aphelios" vs "Aphelios Rapidfire", "Flora Malphite" vs "Malphite AP Flex"). The UI must show mapping coverage (e.g. "Opener rules cover 14/17 BunnyMuffins comps this patch") and list the unmapped ones.
2. **New inputs (small, high-value):** streak selector (Win N / Loss N / Even, default Even) + an optional "2-1 augment was econ?" flag — these two unlock the win/lose-streak branches that the current app cannot express at all. HP/level/gold stay out of v1.
3. **Engine (`OpenerAdvisor`, new module, same shape as `AugmentAdvisor`):** evaluate rules in priority order against the *same* plan object CompFinder uses (owned components, completed items, currentUnits+stars, held augments, emblems owned, streak). Output: `{ direction: 'hard-force' | 'conditional' | 'reroll' | 'flex' | 'lose-streak-econ' | 'none', opener, targetCompIds[], slam[], holdUnits[], avoid[], reasons[] }`. Hard-force/conditional rules fire first and *narrow* the comp list; otherwise the opener returns a direction + slam/hold guidance and CompFinder runs as today.
4. **Feed into the existing recommender (do not replace it):** in `CompFinder.ranked`, add a bounded opener bonus to `fitScore` for target comps (e.g. +15 for a fired hard-force/conditional rule, +8 for a generic-opener lead, 0 otherwise — calibrated in §9 tests, not chosen by feel) *and* surface the opener as its own panel above the ranked list ("Opener: Invoker emblem → Ahri Morgana (hard-force). Slam Shojin. Hold Akali/Camille."). The carousel `discovery` path (no queue) should use `itemPriority.components` (Sword/Rod/Belt) and `slam` order instead of its current top-8-comp heuristic. The anvil "Components" tab and the AugmentAdvisor's econ-augment branch should read the same snapshot (econ-augment list, Worth-the-Wait hit tables) so the three advisors stop disagreeing.
5. **Freshness contract:** the opener panel always shows `Patch 18.3b · BunnyMuffins, updated 2026-10-26 · curated <date>`. If `Academy.snapshot.patch !== opener.patch`, show a banner ("Opener rules are for 18.3b; tierlist is now <patch> — opener guidance may be stale") and demote opener bonuses to 0 (display only). If the snapshot file is missing for the current patch, the opener panel hides itself — it never invents rules.
6. **Update cadence:** per patch, on the same run as the Academy/MetaTFT snapshot refresh. The curation step is ~30–60 min of human reading per patch (mostly transcribing the image boards). Do **not** attempt to automate it with a scraper or a runtime LLM: the value is in the transcribed boards and the explicit comp map, both of which need a human eye. A future step could fetch the page text to *diff* against the previous snapshot and flag changed sections for the curator — that is a build-time aid, not a runtime dependency.

### 8.3 What the opener fixes that CompFinder cannot

- **Stage 1–2 direction before any comp fits.** CompFinder needs completed items/units to score; the opener fires on a single emblem, a single orb unit (Kha'Zix/Rengar), or a single slam (Shojin/Guinsoo's) — the exact inputs a player has at 2-1.
- **Streak-aware planning.** Win-streak → Fast 9; lose-streak → econ + Stage 4 stabilisation. CompFinder has no streak input and its execution penalty *shrinks* when little is entered (§3.5).
- **Slam guidance.** "Slam Shojin, don't greed components" is a decision the current app never makes (it only tracks what you already slammed).
- **Generic boards as a fallback.** When no rule fires, "2 Ravager + Front" (or the best-matching generic opener by owned units) is a better default than alphabetical A-tier (§3.7.1).
